relations.note: Four principal guardians possess halls within the cosmic order culminating in Brahmā’s assembly.
Kubera, Yama, Soma and Varuṇa approach Indra, who confirms their respective cosmic lordships.
The guardians join numerous gods in overpowering and occupying the cosmic being’s body.
relations.source: Matsya Purāṇa; Bṛhat Saṃhitā; architectural manuals

relations.note: The directional guardians surround, praise and attend Śiva as subordinate cosmic powers.
The collective’s northeastern guardian Īśāna is understood as a form or emanation of Śiva.
The guardians attend Viṣṇu, appeal during cosmic crises and enclose Vaiṣṇava ritual diagrams.

relations.myth: Attendance and ritual enclosure of Devī
relations.note: The guardians honor the Goddess and surround her maṇḍalas as subordinate protective powers.
Sūrya enters Manu’s eight and replaces Nirṛti in the southwest in some schemes.
relations.date: c. second century BCE–second century CE

relations.note: Soma enters Manu’s eight and precedes Kubera or Īśāna in northern stations.
relations.date: c. second century BCE–second century CE

relations.note: Brahmā is added above the eight as guardian of the zenith.
Viṣṇu is added below the eight as guardian of the nadir in some lists.
Ananta replaces Viṣṇu as guardian below the eight in some directional systems.
relations.source: Hindu, Jain and tantric directional lists

relations.note: Vāsuki occupies the nadir below the eight in some sectarian directional systems.
Dharaṇendra occupies the nadir below the eight in some Jain directional systems.
